conviction_note: The evidence points both ways. Counterparty demand is positive: AZO's commercial business is +8.6%, ORLY comps +7.2% and SMP reports customer sell-in. The company's own guide arithmetic is negative: Q1 adjusted operating income of $11.2m against an $86-91m FY guide leaves about $25-27m a quarter to find. On this name the reaction has run on EPS and margin, not revenue: in Nov-2025 a revenue beat with an EPS miss traded -26%. So p_up is 48 on a 17-point absolute move (median prior reaction 18.5%), which scales to -0.68. My findings sum to -0.5, so the two measures agree in sign and size.

The quarterly bar has one source, so the reported-quarter findings are capped small.

findings.finding: Q1 FY27 adjusted operating income was $11.2m (GAAP $3.5m), against a reaffirmed FY27 guide of $86-91m. Q2-Q4 must therefore deliver about $75-80m, roughly $25-27m a quarter, more than double the Q1 run-rate. Q1 sales fell 10.8% to $168.0m and net bank debt rose to $99.7m. Holding the guide on Monday needs a visible Q2 step-up. A cut or a 'low end' would land on the line this stock trades on, while consensus FY revenue (~$789.7m) still sits mid-guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Jun-2026, the FY27 guide set at $780-800m: +34.6%. Aug-2026, Q1 miss with the guide reaffirmed: -8.9%. Nov-2025, revenue beat ($221.5m vs $212.2m) with adjusted EPS $0.17 vs $0.39: -26.0% (https://www.chartmill.com/news/MPAA/Chartmill-37475-Motorcar-Parts-of-America-NASDAQMPAA-Reports-Mixed-Q2-2026-Results-with-Revenue-Beat-and-EPS-Miss). Guide and profit lines move this stock by 9-35 points.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. The stock is down ~21.6% since the Q1 print and 8.5% off its 52-week low, and EPS estimates fell ~36% in three months. But consensus FY revenue still sits inside the guide, so the market has marked down the stock without the estimates assuming a guide cut. If the market expected a cut, FY consensus would sit below $780m and the stock would sit at or under its low.
findings.independence: Dorman cut its 2026 sales guide to 2-3% on tariff-pricing margin timing (https://finviz.com/news/408139/dorman-products-inc-reports-third-quarter-2026-results-updates-2026-guidance), a peer supplier to the same retailers. That is a proxy, not this company.

findings.finding: MPAA's largest retail customers and a peer supplier all reported demand inside the Jul-Sep 2026 quarter, after MPAA last spoke on 2026-08-10. AutoZone's domestic commercial same-store sales were +8.6% (total domestic +1.6%, accelerating to +2.1% in August). O'Reilly's Q3 comp was +7.2% and it raised its FY comp guide to 5.5-6.5%. SMP's Vehicle Control segment grew +6.0% on 'strong sell-in as customers deepen assortments to capture DIFM sales'. This supports MPAA's claim that its Q1 shortfall was order timing and that the First Brands liquidation overhang 'has begun to reverse', and it points to Q2 revenue at or above the ~$201m bar.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: This name has sold a revenue beat: Nov-2025 revenue beat by 4% (+6.4% y/y) and the stock traded -26.0% on EPS. Revenue alone has not paid here.
findings.why_not_priced: The stock has not moved on these prints: the 20-day run-up is -0.86% and the 5-day +0.19%. It still trades near its low, as if the Q1 order softness were persisting. If the customer sell-in read were priced, the stock would have retraced part of the 21.6% fall since August.
findings.independence: AutoZone Q4 FY26 release and call (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000866787/000117184326006159/exh_991.htm, 2026-09-22); O'Reilly Q3 2026 (https://finviz.com/news/410690/oreilly-automotive-inc-reports-third-quarter-2026-results, 2026-10-28). These are different documents from SMP's. Against them, Advance Auto Parts' Q3 comps were -1.2%, improving through the quarter (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001158449/000119312526448441/aap-ex99_1.htm). All are proxies: MPAA's own order book is not public.

findings.finding: A peer supplier had a margin problem in the same quarter. Dorman's Q3 2026 light-duty segment margin fell 520bp to 18.5% and it cut its FY sales guide from 3-5% to 2-3%, citing the timing of tariff-related pricing that had flattered Q3 2025. MPAA sells into the same retailers and had $1.4m of net tariff cost in the year-ago Q1. Its Q1 adjusted gross margin was 20.2%, GAAP 16.2%, with a ~2-point FX hit from the peso.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Margin and EPS are the line that has moved MPAA: Nov-2025 EPS miss -26.0%, Aug-2026 EPS miss -8.9%.
findings.why_not_priced: A peer's margin read-across to a two-analyst microcap is not in MPAA's estimates by construction. If it were priced, MPAA would have weakened on Dorman's print, and the 5-day tape is flat.
findings.independence: None from MPAA itself. SMP, also a peer, kept its FY 11-12% adjusted EBITDA margin guide, which cuts the other way (https://finviz.com/news/412581/standard-motor-products-inc-releases-third-quarter-2026-results-and-quarterly-dividend). This is a proxy.

findings.finding: Three companies in this supply chain booked IEEPA tariff refunds in the Jul-Sep 2026 window: SMP received refunds in Q3 and excludes them from adjusted sales, O'Reilly took a $39m benefit, and AutoZone's gross margin benefited. MPAA's FY26 10-K names 'retroactive adjustments, refund claims' under IEEPA as a possibility. Neither the 10-K nor any later filing quantifies a refund (EDGAR full-text search for 'tariff refund' in MPAA filings, 2026: zero hits). Less than 25% of MPAA's products come from China, and its Mexican output is USMCA-exempt. A refund in fiscal Q2 is possible but unquantified, and part may be owed back to customers who absorbed the pass-through.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior MPAA print carried a refund. Its one-time tariff costs (FY25 $5.9m) were excluded from adjusted figures, so a refund is likely excluded from the adjusted line too.
findings.why_not_priced: No MPAA document quantifies it and two analysts are unlikely to model it. If it were priced, the EPS bar would have risen; instead it fell ~36%.
findings.independence: SMP Q3 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000093389/000009338926000098/a991pressrelease-93026.htm); O'Reilly Q3 (https://finviz.com/news/410690/oreilly-automotive-inc-reports-third-quarter-2026-results). Both are proxies for MPAA.

findings.finding: On 2026-06-30 MPAA bought the Centric Parts brake brands (Centric, StopTech, Posi Quiet, C-TEK, GCX) out of First Brands' Chapter 11. The deal covered IP, catalogues and engineering data only, with no operating liabilities, and the business had estimated supplier-level gross sales of up to $400m. Fiscal Q2 is the first full quarter of the relaunch. Management cited 'considerable customer interest' and a target of more than $100m of added annualised sales by year-end, which is excluded from the guide. Any quantified Centric wins on the call would land on the forward run-rate.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Jun-2026, the FY results with the $900m run-rate target announced: +34.6%. Forward new-business statements have moved this stock.
findings.why_not_priced: The stock has fallen ~21.6% since the Q1 call where the relaunch was discussed, so the market is giving the $100m add little credit. If it were priced, the stock would not sit 8.5% off its low with consensus FY revenue mid-guide.
findings.independence: Q1 release language on Centric customer interest (https://investors.motorcarparts.com/news/news-details/2026/Motorcar-Parts-of-America-Reports-Fiscal-2027-First-Quarter-Results). This is the same company, not independent.

findings.finding: Net bank debt rose from $56.7m (Sep-2025) to $99.7m (Jun-2026), and the revolver drew to $118.8m. Q1 used $11.3m of operating cash, mainly an inventory build to $413.3m, alongside buybacks and the Centric purchase. Interest was $12.0m a quarter. The money bought inventory for a stated $100m new-business ramp and the brake brands, and the revolver was extended to Aug-2031. That corroborates a ramp rather than distress, so the financing reads neutral. Q2 cash flow and leverage will be visible on Monday; Nov-2025's release headlined 'strong cash flow, debt reduction'.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No clean isolation. Cash flow was headlined in Nov-2025, a -26% reaction driven by EPS.
findings.why_not_priced: Known since August, so this is mostly a framing item. If Q2 inventory converts to sales, cash flow turns and leverage falls. If not, leverage rises again into a near-low stock.
findings.independence: Shares the Q1 release with the guidance finding; the two are different lines of it. The Sep-2025 debt figure comes from the Nov-2025 release (https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20251110497934/en/Motorcar-Parts-of-America-Reports-Strong-Fiscal-Second-Quarter-Results/).

lessons_applied: Lesson 6 (bar has one source, Yahoo via a search snippet): the reported-quarter proxies were capped smaller. Peer and customer demand went from +1.5 to +1.0, and the Dorman margin read from -1.0 to -0.8.
Lesson 1 (this name sold a revenue beat at -26% in Nov-2025): the revenue finding stays small, and print_vs_bar (+1.5) is allowed to sit apart from a slightly negative expected move.
Lesson 2 (one-offs): the IEEPA refund finding, with no MPAA quantification and likely excluded from adjusted figures, went from +0.5 to +0.3.
Lesson 4 (financing is a question): the debt and inventory build buys a stated ramp plus the Centric brands, with the revolver extended to 2031. Re-signed from -0.5 to 0.0.
Lesson 8 (thin name, understatement): abs_move_pct raised from 16 to 17, toward the 18.5% median reaction.
The guidance finding (-2.0), Centric (+0.5) and positioning (+0.5) were left standing.
